hooks.text: Four astronauts are about to beat Apollo 13's deep space record.
Which upcoming mission will travel farther from Earth than Apollo 13?
After 56 years, four astronauts will finally break Apollo 13's distance record.

title: Artemis II: Beating the Apollo 13 Record
description: NASA's Artemis II mission will send a crew of four 252,756 miles from Earth, surpassing the legendary distance record set by Apollo 13.

beats.text: Four astronauts are about to beat Apollo 13's deep space record.
beats.visual: Official portrait of the Artemis II astronaut crew in flight suits, 2023

beats.text: In April 2026, NASA’s Space Launch System will carry the first crew beyond low Earth orbit since 1972.
beats.visual: Space Launch System rocket on Launch Complex 39B at Kennedy Space Center, 2026

beats.text: Mission specialists Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen will join commander Reid Wiseman and pilot Victor Glover to become the first woman and non-American at the Moon.
beats.visual: Artemis II astronauts during training at NASA Kennedy Space Center, 2024

beats.text: Propelled by the European Service Module, the crew will loop around the lunar far side inside their capsule, Integrity.
beats.visual: Illustration of the Orion spacecraft with the European Service Module in deep space, 2026

beats.text: At its peak, the mission will reach 252,756 miles from home, surpassing any human flight in history.
beats.visual: Illustration of Earth from behind the Moon's far side, 2026
queries: Earth from lunar far side Orion

beats.text: Apollo 13 set its record during a fatal crisis, but Artemis II will do it by design.
beats.visual: Photograph of the damaged Apollo 13 service module after separation, 1970

beats.text: This Pacific splashdown will prove humanity is finally ready to reclaim the Moon.
beats.visual: Orion spacecraft splashdown in the Pacific Ocean during recovery, 2026
